The label the rider tapped does not fix the legal category; the record shows the driver never reached the pickup (F1, F4, F5), so no no-show fee could lawfully arise, and the $5.00 charged on F6 must be refunded in full under NS-2/NS-3 rather than standing under NS-4.

One optimistic reply does not discharge the driver's duties: F3 shows 1 message and 0 calls before cancellation and F1 shows he was still 2137 m away, so he neither satisfied NS-1(iii) nor the NS-8 contact expectation — and his 'About 5 min, traffic' line is contradicted by F12–F14.

This is the driver's own undoing rather than a defence: F1 (never within 200 m), F4 (arrival null) and F5 (no 'I'm Here') mean the chargeable-cancellation preconditions never existed, so the $5.00 must be refunded in full under NS-2/NS-3.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The record fixes who cancelled and when: the rider cancelled at 21:29:20, 200 s (3 min 20 s) after acceptance at 21:26:00, with the app reason "driver_taking_too_long" and a $5.00 fee on record [F2][F6]. Under NS-0 the case runs on the rider-cancellation branch, and NS-4 charges $5.00 for a rider cancellation more than 3 minutes after matching [F2][NS-0][NS-4]. The trace marks both determinations as settled (✓), so no NS-1/NS-2 no-show analysis is triggered: the driver never cancelled [F2].

The rider's core claim is that the arrival conditions of the no-show fee fail — the driver's closest approach was 2137 m, never inside the 200 m radius, arrival was never recorded and "I'm Here" was never tapped [F1][F4][F5]. Those facts are not disputed, but they are conditions of NS-1, which applies only where the DRIVER cancels for a rider no-show [F2][NS-1]. Since the rider cancelled, NS-2 (voiding a no-show fee) has no fee to void, and this is not a "driver cancelled for another reason" case, so NS-3 does not refund either [NS-2][NS-3].

The rider also invokes NS-8 (driver did not arrive). On these facts the rider's free-cancel right under NS-8 is not made out: the driver was in contact within a minute of the rider's question, replying "About 5 min, traffic" at 21:27 [F8][F9], and nothing in the record shows the scheduled pickup time had passed by 5 minutes before the 21:29:20 cancellation [F2]. The 1-message / 0-call contact record and the 2137 m distance are NS-1 prerequisites only — they go to a no-show fee, which was never charged [F3][F1][NS-1].

The driver's "traffic" remark is thin — the speed band on the corridor was 6 (50–59 km/h), no incidents were recorded and conditions were fair and dry [F12][F13][F14] — but an optimistic ETA message does not convert a chargeable rider cancellation into a void fee, and RD-4 exemptions play no part in a no-show dispute [F9][RD-4].

Profiles do not decide the case: the rider's clean record and the driver's one historical upheld no-show dispute are past matters, and no repeat-violation flag (NS-9, RD-6) is triggered here because this was a rider cancellation, not a no-show by the rider or an upheld deviation [F15][F16][NS-9][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 rider-cancellation fee; no refund, no account action against either party on this record. Optionally send the driver a courtesy note on realistic ETAs.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 2137 m at 21:28:55 and he never came within 200 m, so the arrival condition of the no-show fee was never met.
The platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point — driver_arrived_at is null and the driver never tapped "I'm Here" nor was auto-arrival confirmed.
This is not a driver-cancels-for-no-show case at all: the rider cancelled at 21:29:20, 3 min 20 s after acceptance, because the driver was taking too long.

The driver's own message at 21:27 said he was still "About 5 min" away, so the rider's wait had no prospect of ending soon and the driver's written statement that he "was on his way" does not dispute he was still far off.
Even on the driver's best case, only 1 in-app message and 0 in-app calls were made before the cancellation and he never held the pickup point, failing the no-show prerequisites.

The $5.00 cancellation fee was charged (F6) with no surge involved (F7); because the driver was not at the pickup point and had not waited out any free wait, the fee is void and must be refunded in full.

The rider has a clean record (0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days) while the driver already has 1 upheld no-show dispute, so no account flag against the rider is warranted and the driver's no-show conduct is a repeat pattern.

weaknesses: The rider did cancel only 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2), and under NS-4 a rider cancellation after 3 minutes of matching would normally attract the $5.00 fee; the driver's side will argue A1 NS-4 applies. Our answer is NS-1/NS-2 and NS-8: the fee regime for rider cancellation presupposes the driver actually arrived and served the free wait, which the GPS shows he did not (F1, F4, F5).

The app reason recorded is 'driver_taking_too_long' (F2) and the driver wrote that he was on his way (F11) — the driver will cite F11 to argue he was en route and the rider simply gave up; F1 (2137 m away, never inside 200 m) outweighs this as a system record.

The rider's own message "How long will you be?" (F8) shows the rider was aware of the wait and chose to cancel; this goes to willingness to wait, not to whether the driver arrived, and NS-1 requires actual arrival regardless.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled only 3 min 20 s after acceptance, i.e. just past the 3-minute line, and no free-wait or no-show threshold was ever reached because the driver never arrived.

The rider's app-selected cancellation reason was 'driver_taking_too_long', which is a cancellation by the rider (NS-4), not a driver no-show cancellation (NS-1/NS-2); the $5.00 charge is the rider-cancellation fee and no fee was ever transferred to the driver under NS-1.
The driver was en route and in contact: he replied within a minute of the rider's question and told her 'About 5 min, traffic'.

The driver's closed approach to the pickup was 2137 m at 21:28:55, so he never came within the 200 m arrival radius and the platform never recorded an arrival; consequently every condition for voiding a fee under the no-show rules is inapplicable here, because no no-show cancellation occurred.

There is no evidence of traffic congestion justifying a faster approach: the only speed band recorded on the corridor was band 6 (50–59 km/h), no incidents were near the route, and conditions were fair and dry — the driver's 'traffic' message was optimistic, not a misrepresentation that voids anything.
The driver's history over 5.4 years shows 409 trips in 90 days with only 1 upheld dispute (a no-show), so there is no pattern warranting a repeat-violation flag on this record.

weaknesses: F1 and F4–F5 show the driver was 2137 m away, never within 200 m, and never confirmed arrival; the rider will argue the platform's own records show the driver could not realistically have completed the pickup, so the driver's plan for the trip was not dependable.

F9 says 'About 5 min, traffic', but F12–F14 record free-flowing conditions (band 6, no incidents, fair weather), so the rider will use F9 against F12–F14 to attack the driver's credibility about the delay.
F16 shows the driver already has 1 upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days, which the rider will cite under NS-9 as a repeat pattern even though this case is not a no-show.
The driver sent only one message (F3) and made no call, so if the record were re-read as a no-show scenario he could not satisfy NS-1(iii).

points.response: Conceded as to timing only — the rider cancelled 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2) — but D1's own admission that the driver never arrived at all is fatal: NS-1(i) requires actual arrival within 200 m, which F1 and F4 refute, and NS-8 lets a rider cancel free when the driver is not at the pickup and makes no adequate contact.

The label the rider tapped does not fix the legal category; the record shows the driver never reached the pickup (F1, F4, F5), so no no-show fee could lawfully arise, and the $5.00 charged on F6 must be refunded in full under NS-2/NS-3 rather than standing under NS-4.

One optimistic reply does not discharge the driver's duties: F3 shows 1 message and 0 calls before cancellation and F1 shows he was still 2137 m away, so he neither satisfied NS-1(iii) nor the NS-8 contact expectation — and his 'About 5 min, traffic' line is contradicted by F12–F14.

This is the driver's own undoing rather than a defence: F1 (never within 200 m), F4 (arrival null) and F5 (no 'I'm Here') mean the chargeable-cancellation preconditions never existed, so the $5.00 must be refunded in full under NS-2/NS-3.

We agree the road was free-flowing (F12 band 6, F13 no incidents, F14 dry), which is exactly why the driver's claim of 'traffic' (F9) cannot excuse him: RD-4 offers no exemption here and the fee is voided on the arrival failure alone.

No repeat-violation flag is needed for the rider, and the driver's own profile (F16: 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days) sits against the contrasting rider record of 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F15); the profile facts support the refund but do not decide it.

This is true but immaterial: NS-1 applies only where the driver cancels for a rider no-show, and here the record shows the rider cancelled (F2), so the arrival condition never comes into play. The driver does not dispute he was 2137 m away (F1); he disputes that any fee regime was triggered by his own cancellation.

Conceded as fact: the platform recorded no arrival and no "I'm Here" tap (F4, F5). That confirms only that the driver did not cancel for a no-show, which is the driver's own position under NS-0, and it voids nothing, because NS-2 voids a fee only when an NS-1 no-show cancellation fails its conditions.

This is the decisive fact and the driver relies on it: the rider cancelled at 21:29:20, 3 min 20 s after matching (F2), which under NS-4 is a rider cancellation after 3 minutes and therefore carries the $5.00 fee. NS-8 does not apply either, because the driver was never required to be at pickup by scheduled time + 5 min before a rider free-cancel right arose, and the rider's own complaint says she cancelled at just over 3 minutes.

The 21:27 message 'About 5 min, traffic' (F9) is a driver still en route, which is consistent with the rider cancelling mid-approach 2 min 5 s later (F2); it is not an admission of any no-show and the traffic reason given is thin, but a thin reason does not convert a rider cancellation into a void fee under NS-4.

The 1 message / 0 call record (F3) and the 2137 m distance (F1) are NS-1 prerequisites that matter only if the driver had cancelled for a no-show; he did not, so their failure is irrelevant rather than fee-voiding.

NS-2 and NS-3 refund only a no-show fee or a fee charged after a cancellation for another reason; a rider's own post-3-minute cancellation is chargeable under NS-4, and F6/F7 simply show the $5.00 was charged with no surge added.

The driver's 1 upheld historical no-show dispute (F16) is a past matter and under NS-9/RD-6 the profile never decides the current case; the driver's 5.4-year, 409-trip record shows no current repeat conduct to flag.
